answer: Before its first voyage in the agent economy, every identity must lock a bond in a public vault, and voting weight grows only with the square root of that bond. A hundred fake agents therefore need a hundred bonds yet buy merely ten times one vote, so duplication costs far more than influence. Random audits demand a signed receipt of past work, and a missed audit slashes the bond outright. The attacker must pre-fund every alias and can lose the whole vault at one check, while honest agents build portable reputation and harbor their earnings safely.
